Our patient presented with complete penile duplication, epispadias, and a hypoplastic phallus, alongside descended testes (Fig. 1). Initial imaging, including voiding cystourethrogram (VCUG), revealed bladder verticalization (more upright orientation of the bladder outlet axis) and grade 2 vesicoureteral reflux. Untreated neurogenic bladder in children, especially in the context of spinal dysraphism, carries substantial risks of upper urinary tract deterioration and incontinence.

panels.rationale: Single preoperative clinical photograph of the genitalia from a case report titled 'A Rare Case of Isolated Male Epispadias', with caption and overlabeled arrows identifying the abnormally positioned urethral meatus and dorsal cleft - direct manifestations of epispadias.
panels.attribution_text: Shehzad et al. A Rare Case of Isolated Male Epispadias.. Cureus 2023. doi:10.7759/cureus.46160. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: The preoperative anatomy indicating the position of the urethral meatus and dorsal cleft can be appreciated here.
in_text_mentions: tic surgery outpatient department of Holy Family Hospital with complaints of an abnormally located external urethral orifice, micropenis, and urinary incontinence. There was no history of painful micturition, catheterization, family history of epispadias, or any other anomalies. On examination, a single external urethral meatus was found to be located at the junction of the glans and shaft of the penis. Moreover, there was a cleft on the dorsal surface of the glans. The size of the penis was less than normal (Figure 1). The scrotum, testis, abdominal, and rectal examinations were unremarkable.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (Voiding 1, Voiding 2). Voiding 1: Filling-phase voiding cystourethrogram of a real patient in a case report whose disease-focused title and caption explicitly state epispadias ('urethra ... except for mild epispadias'); the pelvis and contrast-filled lower tract are shown, so the panel is a genuine patient radiograph demonstrating the target condition. Other findings (VUR, smooth wall, diverticulum) are noted as proposed because they are not in the allowed vocabulary. Voiding 2: Voiding-phase radiograph of the same real patient; the caption attributes the only urethral abnormality to mild epispadias, a configured target disease, and the article title is epispadias-focused. Kept as a patient radiograph of the target condition; findings beyond the vocabulary are recorded as proposed.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Preoperative clinical photograph of the reported male epispadias patient; caption and in-text description directly identify the dorsal penopubic meatus and abnormal penile morphology, which are core manifestations of epispadias. The morphology is described as unusual in the article title, hence variant. B: Clinical photograph demonstrating the wide, dorsally sited external urethral meatus, explicitly stated in the caption and corroborated by the in-text description of incontinence from a wide-open penopubic meatus — a classic epispadias finding.
panels.attribution_text: Tampubolon and Sibarani. Unusual morphology of isolated male epispadia: A rare case report.. Urology case reports 2024. doi:10.1016/j.eucr.2024.102707. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: (A) Preoperative morphology of epispadia. (b) The wide opening of the external meatus.

The wide-open meatus in the penopubic area led to urinary incontinence from birth. The patient underwent pelvic MRI which revealed the absence of a penis and diastasis of the pubic symphysis.
